baseline.reason:
Exact bug and unaffected output lines matched the shared three-version Docker replay.; Root cause: commit 4b136ed70a1e marks the FTS3/4 virtual table module SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS (fts3DeclareVtab in ext/fts3/fts3.c), lowering its eVtabRisk from SQLITE_VTABRISK_Normal(1) to Low(0). This is checked by vtabIsReadOnly() in src/delete.c (applied when pParse->pToplevel!=0, i.e. inside a trigger) and by the fromDDL gate in src/select.c, both comparing "pTab->u.vtab.p->eVtabRisk" against "(db->flags & SQLITE_TrustedSchema)!=0". Before the change, any nested (triggered) write to an FTS3/4 table was refused outright when trusted_schema=OFF, because eVtabRisk(1) > trustedSchema(0). After the change, eVtabRisk(0) is no longer greater than 0, so the nested write is allowed to proceed into FTS4's own xUpdate, which internally calls sqlite3_prepare_v2() on a dynamically built "SELECT <funcname>(?)" statement using the schema-supplied compress=/uncompress= function name. That internally generated statement is indistinguishable from ordinary trusted top-level SQL and is not flagged as derived from DDL, so the "disallow unsafe SQL functions" check silently does not apply to it, letting a non-innocuous application function run even though trusted_schema=OFF was supposed to prevent exactly that in untrusted/nested schema contexts. The companion fix commit (add73c831bfe, mirroring upstream check-in 26f39ac806 which adds the SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL flag) propagates the DDL/untrusted-origin context into these internally-generated FTS3/4 statements so the unsafe-function check correctly applies to them.

Verified by direct reproduction in Docker (ASan/UBSan build) using the identical PoC/command across all three revisions:
- pre_intro (commit a11499a1566f, FTS3 NOT yet innocuous): the nested trigger-INSERT into the FTS4 table is refused outright with "unsafe use of virtual table \"f1\"" before ever reaching the compress function; the exact output line "RESULT: rc=1 myfunc_invoked=0" is printed. Bug not present/not reachable — behaves safely.
- post_intro (commit 4b136ed70a1e, FTS3 marked SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS): the nested write succeeds and the untrusted application function myfunc() is actually invoked via the compress hook despite trusted_schema=OFF; the exact output line "RESULT: rc=0 myfunc_invoked=1" is printed (this line/behavior never appears in pre_intro or post_benign). This is the labelled logic-error/security-check bypass, reproduced live.
- post_benign (fix commit, composed via agent to match upstream add73c831bfe/26f39ac806): the nested write is blocked again with "SQL logic error" (the unsafe-function check now correctly fires on the internally generated compress statement); the exact output line "RESULT: rc=1 myfunc_invoked=0" is printed again, matching pre_intro. Bug is fixed.

The same exact PoC/command was used unmodified across all three builds, and the result cleanly differs: safe -> bug -> fixed, satisfying the required behavioral oracle for a LogicError-class protection bypass.

oracle.description: C program (poc.c) using the sqlite3 C API, linked against the built amalgamation (gcc -fsanitize=address,undefined ... sqlite3.c poc.c). It registers a plain (non-innocuous) application SQL function `myfunc`, creates an ordinary table `src`, an FTS4 virtual table `f1` configured with `compress=myfunc, uncompress=myfunc`, and an AFTER INSERT trigger on `src` that performs a nested `INSERT INTO f1(rowid,x) VALUES(new.id,new.val)`. It then sets `PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF` and issues a top-level `INSERT INTO src VALUES(1,'one two three')`, which fires the trigger and causes a *nested* write into the FTS4 vtab — exactly the scenario SQLite's trusted-schema vtab-risk gate (vtabIsReadOnly in delete.c, applied when pParse->pToplevel!=0) and the unsafe-function gate are meant to police. The harness counts invocations of myfunc via a global counter to detect whether the untrusted function actually ran.
oracle.target_evidence: Confirmed via grep that post_intro's ext/fts3/fts3.c contains `sqlite3_vtab_config(p->db, SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS);` in fts3DeclareVtab while pre_intro does not. Confirmed the enforcement code paths in src/delete.c (vtabIsReadOnly, checked when pParse->pToplevel!=0, i.e. inside triggers) and src/select.c (fromDDL gate), both comparing `pTab->u.vtab.p->eVtabRisk` against `(db->flags & SQLITE_TrustedSchema)!=0`, matching SQLITE_VTABRISK_Normal=1/Low=0/High=2 constants in sqliteInt.h. This matches the official upstream disclosure (sqlite.org check-in 26f39ac806) and the saved regression tests (evidence/test_01_..._fts3comp1.test section 3, and test_02_..._fts4content.test section 13) which test the same unsafe-function-via-untrusted-schema class of bug for FTS3/4. Full run outputs captured via run_poc for pre_intro, post_intro, and post_benign with the identical poc.c/run.sh.
